entries.title: DRAFT: why metric KPZ needs field independence
entries.statement: Unreviewed campaign deduction from Gwynne-Pfeffer Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.7. Fix gamma in (0,2), a whole-plane GFF h and a nonempty deterministic planar domain U. Write Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and xi=gamma/d_gamma for the canonical gamma-LQG metric D_h. The gamma-thick points X in U have Euclidean Hausdorff dimension 2-gamma^2/2 and D_h dimension d_gamma almost surely. Applying the independent-set equality dim_E X=xi Q dim_D X-(xi^2/2)(dim_D X)^2 to this field-dependent X instead gives 2; the residual is gamma^2/2. At gamma=sqrt(8/3), applying that equality to a nonconstant D_h-geodesic of intrinsic dimension 1 would instead give Euclidean dimension 3/4, whereas a connected continuous image with distinct endpoints has Euclidean dimension at least 1 by a Lipschitz distance projection. These are obstructions to deleting independence, not values of the general d_gamma.
assumptions: Known d_sqrt(8/3)=4 for the geodesic control

entries.title: DRAFT: diagonal soft-min bias and endpoint cancellation
entries.statement: Unreviewed finite-Gaussian control. For each integer n>=1 set L_n=beta_n=n and K_n=2^(n^2). Take K_n distinct singleton paths of unit weights whose centered Gaussian fields all equal one common standard normal Z. The covariance is PSD with maximum diagonal 1. At fixed xi>=0 the hard log minimum is xi Z, but the soft minimum F_beta=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp(-beta f_p) equals xi Z-n log 2 at beta_n=n. Thus normalized expectations differ by -log 2 although beta_n tends to infinity. This attains the absolute smoothing error bound. The bias does not depend on xi and cancels in endpoint differences; this control alone does not refute an integrated endpoint reduction.
assumptions: Finite path model; no planar LFPP realization claimed
entries.domain: probability / LQG / finite Gaussian path controls

entries.title: DRAFT: integrated response needs uniform smoothing control
entries.statement: Unreviewed analytic finite-Gaussian counterexample. For n>=1 let L_n=beta_n=n and M_n=2^(n^2). Take M_n distinct singleton paths with deterministic zero Gaussian fields and weight exp(n), plus one path with M_n independent N(0,n) fields and vertex weights 1/M_n. The centered Gaussian covariance is PSD diagonal with maximum variance v_n=n=O(L_n). Put f_n(xi)=log[(1/M_n) sum_i exp(xi sqrt(n) Z_i)] and H_n(xi)=min(n,f_n(xi)). The beta_n soft minimum is F_n(xi)=-(1/n)log[exp(-n^2(1-log 2))+exp(-n f_n(xi))]. At endpoints xi=0 and xi=2, the normalized hard expected difference tends to 1, while the normalized soft expected difference tends to 1-log 2. The hard medians at those endpoints are 0 and n for all sufficiently large n. For S_n=exp(f_n(2)), its mean is exp(2n), relative variance is (exp(4n)-1)/M_n, and Jensen bounds its negative logarithmic part using 2 sqrt(n) Z_bar; these bounds prove the stated limits. The fixed-network Gaussian interpolation integral equals the soft endpoint difference. Therefore beta_n->infinity, v_n=O(L_n), and convergent hard-min endpoint medians do not by themselves justify the integrated reduction. This is a general finite-path control, not a planar LFPP computation.
assumptions: Finite family of nonempty paths with positive deterministic weights
Independent long-path Gaussian coordinates of variance n

entries.title: DRAFT: sufficient entropy control for a finite-to-scale reduction
entries.statement: Unreviewed bridge checklist. For a finite nonempty family of real path log costs f_p(y), beta>0 and K paths, define H(y)=min_p f_p(y) and F_beta(y)=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp(-beta f_p(y)). Then 0<=H(y)-F_beta(y)<=log K/beta for every y. For growing families, L_n->infinity and log K_n/(beta_n L_n)->0 therefore suffice for normalized expected endpoint differences to agree whenever the hard endpoint limits exist and the costs are integrable. A sharper effective-entropy estimate may replace this sufficient condition. The finite Gaussian response identity also requires retaining the negative beta times covariance of path gradients; its two nonnegative pieces cannot be separated or discarded just because one route wins almost surely. Neither the entropy bound nor concentration evaluates the actual planar-LFPP normalization exponent.
assumptions: Uniform entropy error tends to zero for the stated transfer
entries.domain: probability / LQG / finite Gaussian path controls

relations.rationale: Absolute control: 'bias does not depend on xi and cancels'. Integrated control: endpoint limits are '1' and '1-log 2'. The second construction supplies the endpoint distinction missing from the first.
The control has log K_n/(beta_n L_n) tending to log 2, while the sufficient bridge explicitly requires that ratio to tend to zero. The control is excluded by the bridge premise.

Poincare card: 'f be locally Lipschitz with f and its gradient in L^2'. The finite path minimum is globally sqrt(v_n) times xi Lipschitz in standard Gaussian coordinates and integrable; variance concentration still does not fix its soft-min bias.

Gaussian card: 'X is centred Gaussian' and differentiability with 'appropriate integrability'. At every fixed finite n and beta_n the smooth path objective has bounded derivatives, so the interpolation integral equals its soft endpoint difference, which this control computes.

Prior attempt: 'It does not calculate xi for other parameters.' Current checklist: concentration and uniform smoothing do not evaluate the actual planar-LFPP exponent. Both preserve the same unresolved numerical metric bridge.

Problem card asks for the 'almost sure Hausdorff dimension d_gamma'. The dependent-set controls invalidate uses of independent KPZ that would purport to calculate that metric dimension; they leave the target unresolved.
